item.title: [BoSox Injection] Red Sox Injury Update: Justin Slaten disappointment, Kristian Campbell twist, Romy Gonzalez

item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox could have a slew of pitching reinforcements returning before the playoffs begin, including Tanner Houck, Garrett Crochet, and maybe even Johan Oviedo and Kutter Crawford. Justin Slaten will not be among them.
Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy on September 15 told reporters (including Tim Healey of The Boston Globe) that Slaten got a PRP injection in his arm to address a flexor issue. His season is over after multiple attempts to ramp up for a rehab assignment and eventual return.
Slaten has been quite injury prone over his three years with the Red Sox. He went on the injured list for the first time this season in early April and didn't return until mid-May. For the second straight year, he'll finish his season with less than 35 innings pitched.
Justin Slaten's season with Red Sox ends after he gets PCP injection for flexor injury
The righty has dabbled in the extremes this season, finishing with a 4.60 ERA over 31.1 innings. In June, Slaten's worst month this year, he allowed nine runs on 17 hits over 11 outings. July was his best, during which he let up just one run on five hits over nine appearances. His WHIP has starkly increased over the past year, from 1.09 in 2025 to 1.37.
When the Red Sox can get Slaten's best, he's one of the biggest threats out of their bullpen. But he's often injured or prone to blowups that keep him from showing the best he can offer. It will be interesting to see his role next season when Boston has more healthy pitching depth it could push to the bullpen.
Red Sox confirm Kristian Campbell's season is over due to foot injury, ending breakout
Kristian Campbell's season has also ended prematurely due to an injury. The outfielder will be out for the rest of the year due to a left foot contusion, according to Tommy Cassell of the Worcester Telegram & Gazette.
The WooSox pulled Campbell from their September 8 game due to the injury. Even before the announcement of his IL stint, it was evident that Campbell's season could be over, as Worcester's last regular season game is on Septembet 20.
Campbell's injury ends a resurgent second half for the 24 year old. He slashed .311/.430/.497 over 51 games after the All-Star break and, had he been healthy, he might've been selected to come up and help the major league team while Ceddanne Rafaela and Eli White are injured.
Romy Gonzalez continues tear following arm injury scare with WooSox
On the same day Campbell was pulled from the WooSox's lineup, Romy Gonzalez was, too. An arm injury led to a week on the shelf for the utility infielder, but he joined the Triple-A lineup again on September 15.
Gonzalez has resumed the tear he was on before his arm flared up. He logged two hits, including a double, in his return and boosted his September slash line to .500/.520/.727 over six games. Gonzalez has hit so well lately that it could be time to call him back up to the major leagues to give Boston's slumping offense a boost.

item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox got some bad news on Tuesday. Top prospect Kristian Campbell is going on the IL, which means his season is over.
Campbell was with the Worcester Red Sox at the Triple-A level. There, he suffered a foot contusion, per Tommy Cassell.
In 109 games with the WooSox, Campbell has a .256 average this season with a .763 OPS. That’s with 8 home runs, 51 RBIs, and 73 walks. Defensively, he’s spent most of his time in the outfield. That’s despite largely playing second base in 2025.
Notably, Campbell was showing improvement in the second half. In 36 games since the All-Star break, he was hitting .333 with a 1.009 OPS, to go along with 6 home runs. That had, seemingly, made him an option to come up to the majors.
Kristian Campbell Didn’t Play for the Boston Red Sox in 2026
In 2025, Kristian Campbell made the Boston Red Sox roster coming out of Spring Training. He was the Opening Day second baseman, and there was a lot of excitement about what he could end up being.
Things didn’t work out. In 67 games, he hit .223 with a .664 OPS. Campbell had 6 home runs and 21 RBIs. To go along with those offensive struggles, he was a bit of a liability defensively at second base. So, the Red Sox would often play him in the outfield, but they already have a logjam of players there.
Eventually, Campbell was sent to Triple-A to work on improving his swing and to find a defensive position. That’s where he’d spend the entire season.
At the MLB level, the Red Sox have had some injury issues. That’s forced them, at times, to lean on players who would normally be bench players or borderline players between Triple-A and the majors. However, they resisted rushing Campbell back to Boston, after seemingly rushing him in 2025. With his improving bat as of late, there was some excitement that he could be returning to the majors soon, but that’s not going to happen now.
The Future for the Red Sox and Campbell
While it may seem strange for Campbell to be away from the MLB team for so long, his future with the Red Sox is still bright.
Campbell is finishing up his age 24 season. He’s still relatively young and when he does get his next chance with the Red Sox, he’ll better know what to expect at the MLB level, and he’ll be going to that level with more development under his belt.
The Red Sox and Campbell are also committed to one another. In April of 2025, the Red Sox signed Campbell to an eight-year, $60 million contract. So, he’s going to be with Boston for the foreseeable future, regardless of the upcoming CBA changes.
The challenge now for Boston is to find what position Campbell will play when he rejoins the MLB team. There’s still a logjam in the outfield. Campbell still isn’t viewed as a great option defensively, and those infield spots are filling quickly. So, will a move be made to clear space for Campbell?

item.content:encoded:
Boston Red Sox fans will not be seeing former top prospect Kristian Campbell in the big leagues at all this season, unfortunately.
On Tuesday, Tommy Cassell of the Worcester T&G Sports reported that Campbell's season is over. Campbell was placed on the seven-day Injured List due to a left foot contusion on Sep. 10. Cassell reported that Campbell will not be able to return before Triple-A Worcester's season ends on Sep. 20.
"Some injury updates today in AAA Worcester: Tanner Houck is scheduled to pitch one inning (20-25 pitches) in relief," Cassell wrote. "Romy Gonzalez is in at DH despite being a bit banged up. Iggy Suarez mentioned he's "an option" to contribute with the Red Sox moving forward. Kristian Campbell is out for the rest of the WooSox season. 'He was a big part of what we've been doing,' Suarez said. 'So, it's definitely a downer for that.'"
Kristian Campbell Is Done For The Year
That's some really unfortunate news for one of the most intriguing players in the Red Sox's system. Campbell made the big league club out of Spring Training in 2025 as the first member of the "Big 3," including him, Roman Anthony and Marcelo Mayer. He was red-hot out of the gate to the point that Boston handed him an eight-year, $60 million deal. But things took a turn afterward. Campbell was demoted to Triple-A in June, 2025. He hasn't been in the majors since.
Campbell played in 73 down in Triple-A last season and then didn't make the Red Sox's big league club out of camp. He has been down in the minors all season this year trying to work his way back.
The 24-year-old spent the season in the outfield as Boston tried to slow things down after moving him around all over the place last year. For Boston, it is loaded in the outfield to the point that there was a logjam early on in the season. Then, despite the Red Sox losing Roman Anthony to the Injured List for a while, there still wasn't space for Campbell in the majors.
Overall, Campbell wrapped up his season after playing in 109 games for Triple-A and slashing .256/.383/.380 with a .763 OPS, eight homers and 51 RBIs. Hopefully, he's able to get back on track and get back into the mix by the time Spring Training rolls around. Who could've seen this coming back in 2025? Campbell looked like a franchise cornerstone piece. Unfortunately, he hasn't been in the majors in over a year and now that won't be happening this year.
